solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sheep does in time enter wind on returning

indicators.note: to enter something is to go inside it, so the killing word and the time letter go inside the turned-round word
something returning comes back the way it went, so the word for wind is read from its far end

parts.note: to reel is to wind, as with a fishing line
to ice someone is slang for to kill, to do them in
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A gruesome farmyard image: something kills off does and then a wind blows back over the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' looks like female deer, but it is the verb in the slang phrase 'does in', to kill.
explanation.definitionFit: The Leicester is an English breed of long-wool sheep, named after the county where it was developed.

clue.text: Some flipping kiss

indicators.note: some of a word is only part of it, so the answer is a run of letters inside

parts.note: letters two to four of the word

explanation.surface: An exasperated remark about a bit of a blasted kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a reversal signal, but the answer reads forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Lip as a verb means to touch with the lips, that is, to kiss, in literary use.

clue.text: Yankee charm? Long hair curled up on Republican

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from the bottom, so the word for hair runs backwards

parts.note: a mane is a long head of hair
o' is a short form of on, as in o'clock
R abbreviates Republican

explanation.surface: A Republican politician's coiffed mane, presented as American charm.
explanation.walkthrough: Yankee signals the American spelling, without the U.
explanation.definitionFit: To enamor is to charm or captivate, spelt in the American way.

clue.text: Crow (boast, as some would say)

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a crow or raven, in dialect
second meaning: a dialect verb meaning to brag

explanation.walkthrough: 'Crow' looks like the verb brag, which would make both halves mean the same; here it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: In dialect the word names a crow and also means to boast; 'as some would say' marks the regional usage.

clue.text: In short form just ringing Geneva's source of power

indicators.note: ringing something surrounds it like a ring, so the spirit sits inside the other word

parts.note: ene is a contracted form of even, which means just
Geneva is an old name for gin, from the Dutch genever

explanation.surface: Brief talk about a Swiss city's power supply, as though Geneva were the source.
explanation.walkthrough: Geneva is not the Swiss city but the old name for gin; 'just' means even, as in 'even so'.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine is a machine that converts energy into motion, a source of mechanical power.

clue.text: Loosely as per temptation and behind time lose lucky charm?

indicators.note: loosely means without fixed order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a dap is a bait bobbed on the water to tempt fish
behind time means late

explanation.surface: A gambler running late who misplaces a good-luck token.
explanation.walkthrough: A racehorse spreads a plate when it loses a shoe, and a horseshoe is a lucky charm; hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A plate is a light racing horseshoe, and horseshoes are traditional good-luck symbols, so losing one fits.

clue.text: Raising a glass to stern foil for Errol Flynn, for example

definitions.text: foil for Errol Flynn, for example

parts.note: drinking a toast to someone
iron means hard and unbending, as in an iron will

explanation.surface: Drinking to a stern opponent, a foil or rival for the swashbuckling film star Errol Flynn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foil' suggests a rival who shows off the star, but it is a fencing sword; Flynn was famous for sword-fighting roles.
explanation.definitionFit: Toasting iron is a facetious old term for a sword, likening it to a fire tool for toasting.

clue.text: Couple in Macao maybe running up brooms and the like

indicators.note: in a down entry, running up means reading from the bottom, so letters go backwards
in puts the word for couple inside the territory's label

parts.note: Macao is a Special Administrative Region of China, an SAR
to mate is to couple or pair

explanation.surface: A couple in Macao running up a hill among broom bushes.
explanation.walkthrough: Macao, like Hong Kong, is a Special Administrative Region of China, abbreviated SAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Retama is a genus of Mediterranean shrubs related to broom; the word is also used for such brooms.

clue.text: Provide love for the image of Scots innocence

parts.note: to do is to provide, as a caterer does lunches
love is nil in tennis, so the round zero letter

explanation.surface: A charity appeal: give some love towards what stands for Scottish innocence.
explanation.walkthrough: DOO is the Scots word for a dove, the traditional image of innocence and peace.
explanation.definitionFit: The dove is the conventional emblem of innocence, and DOO is the Scottish dialect name for that bird.

clue.text: Takes great risks accepting schmutter in orders

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so the cloth word goes inside

parts.note: one who dices with death takes great risks
schmutter is Yiddish-derived slang for rubbish or cheap clothes, i.e. tat

explanation.surface: A gambler who accepts shoddy rags as payment when following instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: Schmutter is British slang from Yiddish for rags or junk; tat is cheap tasteless stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Dictates are commands or authoritative orders that must be obeyed.

clue.text: Hearsay from second I trust

indicators.note: from means taken out of, so the letters come out of the words that follow

parts.note: the run spans the end of second, I, and the start of trust

explanation.surface: Gossip from a second source that one trusts.
explanation.definitionFit: An on-dit is a piece of gossip, from the French for 'it is said', so rumour.

clue.text: In stirring manner erode most plated protection?

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Something that wears away most of a plated covering when stirred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stirring' suggests rousing, but it is the mixing sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An osteoderm is a bony plate in the skin, as in crocodiles and armadillos, serving as armour.

clue.text: Lay to rest wearing uniform which signifies the senior service

indicators.note: a person wearing clothes has them on, so the one-word piece sits around the next letter here

parts.note: dressed in something is wearing it
Uniform is U in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the Royal Navy is called the senior service, being the oldest of Britain's armed forces

explanation.surface: A naval funeral in which the sailor is buried wearing dress uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wearing' does double work in the surface but simply gives IN; the senior service is the Royal Navy, the oldest British armed force.
explanation.definitionFit: To inurn is to place ashes in an urn, a way of burying or laying the dead to rest.

clue.text: Round wreaths laid round new compounds

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

indicators.note: something laid round another thing encircles it, so the garlands are placed on either side of the next letter

parts.note: leis are Hawaiian flower garlands
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Circular wreaths placed around something new, as at an unveiling.
explanation.definitionFit: Oleins are chemical compounds: glycerides of oleic acid found in fats and oils.

clue.text: Verbal fun from soldier close to trouble no longer

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper
an obsolete word for grief or trouble, long since only a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A soldier's banter is the only fun left now that trouble is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer' marks an obsolete sense: GRAM once meant trouble or grief.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragram is a pun formed by altering a letter of a word, a kind of verbal wordplay.

clue.text: Fare from Abroath that is fine, initially found in text service

indicators.note: something found in a place lies inside it, so the earlier pieces sit within the messaging abbreviation

parts.note: SMS, short message service, is mobile phone texting
OK means fine, and 'initially' puts it first in the inserted group
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A food blogger approving of a dish from Arbroath, said in a text message.
explanation.walkthrough: Arbroath (spelt Abroath here) is a fishing town in eastern Scotland famous for its smoked haddock.
explanation.definitionFit: Arbroath smokies are haddock smoked whole over hardwood, the town's famous local dish.

clue.text: Discharge old quitter in supplement for all to see cost

parts.note: supp. abbreviates supplement
U is the film rating meaning suitable for everyone
a rate is a charge or cost

explanation.surface: Sacking a deserter, with the cost made public in a newspaper supplement.
explanation.walkthrough: Quitter is not a deserter but an old word for pus, so the definition means to discharge pus.
explanation.definitionFit: To suppurate is to form and discharge pus, which quitter meant in older English.

clue.text: Murphy thanks with bow

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks
a bow is a tie, as in bow tie

explanation.surface: Someone called Murphy says thanks and bows politely.
explanation.walkthrough: Murphy is slang for a potato (from the Irish surname), and TATIE is the Scots word for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal names for the potato: murphy from Irish associations, tatie from Scots dialect.

clue.text: Unsettled fate lies in restricted estates

indicators.note: unsettled means disturbed, so the letters are not left in place

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An uncertain destiny lies in property with legal restrictions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unsettled' also echoes settled estates in law, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: A fee tail is an estate in land whose inheritance is limited to a particular line of heirs.

clue.text: In addition coaster ferried in fruit

indicators.note: a cargo ferried in is carried inside a vessel, so the table mat sits inside the other word

parts.note: too means also, in addition
a coaster is a small mat for a glass

explanation.surface: A small coastal ship carries fruit cargo as well as other goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coaster' suggests a coastal ship, but it is the drinks mat.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically the tomato is a fruit, a berry bearing seeds, though usually cooked as a vegetable.

clue.text: Ready for theatre? It's planned where first time is close to epic

indicators.note: this says the earliest time letter is swapped out and something else stands where it was

parts.note: premeditated means planned in advance
T abbreviates time; the first one in the word is replaced

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is used

parts.note: the last letter of epic

explanation.surface: A wry line about an operation scheduled in advance, with a nod to epic drama in the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: Theatre here is the operating theatre, not the stage, which is why the definition carries a question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A premedicated patient has been given sedative drugs before surgery, so is prepared for the operating room.

clue.text: Priest holds up sacred text for mischievous charmer

indicators.note: in a down entry, holding something up means supporting it from below, so the priest's letter comes last

parts.note: a mantra is a sacred verbal formula, as in Hindu scripture
P abbreviates priest

explanation.surface: A priest supporting a holy text against a beguiling tempter.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'holds up' puts the priest underneath, at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantrap is informally a seductive woman, a charmer who ensnares men.

clue.text: Flower — tag for such in fellah's window

indicators.note: in places the single letter inside the phrase that follows it

parts.note: a fellah is an Egyptian peasant, and the eye is called the window of the soul

indicators.note: a tag is a tail end, so only the closing letter of the following word is wanted

parts.note: the final letter of such

explanation.surface: A gardener's label for a flower, seen through the window of a peasant's hut.
explanation.walkthrough: A fellah is an Arab or Egyptian peasant; the eye as window of the soul is a familiar phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Pheasant's eye is the name of a red-flowered adonis and also of a white narcissus.

clue.text: Maori prize that's most often seen in waka in Pacific kingdom

indicators.note: the second in places the chosen letter inside the kingdom's name

parts.note: Tonga is a Polynesian kingdom in the Pacific

indicators.note: the letter that appears most often in the word is the one taken

parts.note: this letter occurs twice in waka, more than any other

explanation.surface: A Maori trophy usually displayed in a canoe from a Pacific island kingdom.
explanation.walkthrough: A waka is a Maori canoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Taonga is the Maori word for a treasure or anything highly prized.

clue.text: Cautious consent still restricting transport with tail fully lifted

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the vehicle is held inside the other word
in a down entry, lifting the tail all the way moves the last letter up to the top

parts.note: yet means still, as in 'still to come'
a bus is public transport

explanation.surface: A reluctant yes while a vehicle is towed with its rear raised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fully lifted' means the last letter travels all the way to the top of the down entry, not just one place.
explanation.definitionFit: A yes-but is an agreement with a reservation attached, a hedged form of assent.

clue.text: Masculine one from Provence is down to release catch

parts.note: un is the French masculine word for one, and 's stands for is
nap is the soft downy surface of fabric

explanation.surface: A Provençal man is reduced to letting go of a fastening.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsnap is to undo a snap fastener, freeing a catch.

clue.text: What's in shells concerning sub's attacker up above

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an ashcan is naval slang for a depth charge, used against submarines
re means concerning

explanation.surface: A naval question about what lies inside the shells fired at submarines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shells' suggests ammunition alongside the sub, but it means seashells.
explanation.definitionFit: Nacre is mother-of-pearl, the iridescent lining of mollusc shells.

clue.text: Dig fabulous creature, old beau taking number for Prince

indicators.note: taking one thing for another means it replaces it in the word

parts.note: spark is an old word for a gallant suitor
N is the abbreviation for number
P abbreviates prince

explanation.surface: A dig at a mythical beast's old flame, who swapped a prince for a mere number.
explanation.walkthrough: The Snark is the imaginary beast of Lewis Carroll's The Hunting of the Snark.
explanation.definitionFit: A snark is a snide remark, a dig, and also Carroll's fabulous imaginary creature.

clue.text: Ill-behaved but beginning to be irritable

indicators.note: but can mean except or without, so something is left out

parts.note: behaving like a spoilt brat

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only that is taken

parts.note: the first letter of be

explanation.surface: A badly behaved child who is starting to be cranky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'But' reads as a contrast but means without here.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty is informal British for bad-tempered or easily annoyed.

clue.text: Hero worship is happening first in most of southern capital

indicators.note: in places the earlier words inside the shortened city name
most of something is all but its final part, so the last letter goes

parts.note: Lima is the capital of Peru, in the southern hemisphere
an event on is happening
taken as written

explanation.surface: A personality cult flourishing first in a South American capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' only fixes the order of the two short words; the southern capital is Lima, in Peru.
explanation.definitionFit: Lionism is the treating of people as celebrities or lions, that is, idolising them.

clue.text: Palm one toiling for Indian in Hispanic hotspot, once

indicators.note: in puts the animal's name inside the name of the island

parts.note: a Spanish-speaking island that was a Cold War flashpoint
the arna is the Indian water buffalo, a draught animal

explanation.surface: An Indian labourer working in a Latin American trouble spot of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One toiling for Indian' looks like a worker but is a beast of burden, the arna or water buffalo.
explanation.definitionFit: The carnauba is a Brazilian wax palm whose leaves yield carnauba wax.

clue.text: Apparent term for epigone

parts.note: ap. abbreviates apparent, as in heir apparent

indicators.note: a term is a limit or end, so only the closing letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the final letter of epigone

explanation.surface: A lexicographer offering an obvious word for a slavish follower of a master.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: read straight, it asks for an obvious word for an imitator.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigone is an inferior imitator of a master, and an ape is one who copies or mimics.

clue.text: Having three "points" current in pamphlet

indicators.note: in places the electrical symbol inside the word for a leaflet

parts.note: a tract is a short pamphlet
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A pamphlet making three topical points.
explanation.definitionFit: Triact describes a sponge spicule with three rays, the 'points' of the definition.

clue.text: Where lots go in Scotland following grand mass

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the Scottish sale word is placed after the single letter

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars
a roup is a Scottish auction, where lots are sold

explanation.surface: A Scottish sale where a lot of grand items go, all following one after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lots' means auction lots, not a large amount.
explanation.definitionFit: A group and a mass are both a gathering or collection of things together.

clue.text: Henry with this devious devil would be one to let down

indicators.note: the clue says adding a letter to the answer gives another word, so the answer is that word minus the letter

parts.note: a heel is a cad, someone who lets people down
H is the symbol of the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A man named Henry, teamed with a sly rogue, would prove a letdown.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer joined to H would make HEEL, so remove H from HEEL.
explanation.definitionFit: An eel is a slippery, evasive person, hard to pin down and so devious.

clue.text: Quartzy mineral he kept in a transfer

indicators.note: a transfer moves things to new positions, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man held on to a mineral sample during a move.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenakite is a beryllium silicate mineral that resembles quartz, hence its name meaning deceiver.
